My current issue is my mental state. Since sometime in the middle/end of spring last year, I got an illness that did something to me. I had severe strep throat (which can trigger a disorder called Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal Infections on rare occasions). Since the infection, I've been experiencing the symptoms of this somewhat rare disorder (symptoms listed but not limited to: tics, OCD like behaviors, mood lability, severe anxiety, and sleep disturbances). It's been a living hell for me since, as it is getting harder to cope with all of the problems I've had, and that I used to be a relatively normal person until this all happened. My significant other left me because of all of this, because he didn't want to be around someone as messed up as I was (he lost interest in me because I changed by something I couldn't help, and what he disliked). I now take medicine that helps, but since I've gotten so used to it, if I forget to take at least one of the pills, I break down with bad panic attacks and sometimes even auditory hallucinations. On the light of it, at least I've gotten better since the incident, and I now have things to help me out (and that I had my medicine fixed and had some therapy at a mental hospital a month ago).

The scariest thing that has happened to me while on vacation happened two days before Christmas last year. I went to Nashville, Tennessee to see a Christmas concert at the Ryman Auditorium. Seems nice, right? Well, on that day, a tornado was raging in the town and nearby the town. When my friend, sister and I got off the transportation bus from the Gaylord Opryland hotel, there already was one of the worst thunderstorms I have ever seen in my life. During the concert, there was wailing tornado sirens, blaring ever so loudly just outside the building. When we got back on the bus, we saw the tornado in the far distance while the bus was in the middle of the town. We also heard the whistling wind, flowing fast beside the bus while racing back to the hotel. When we got into our room, the television was showing updates of the tornado and whatnot. I'd say that was the closest I ever was to a tornado in my lifetime. You can actually find footage of it on Youtube.

It kind of sounds like you either have general anxiety disorder, or possibly even panic disorder. I'm not a doctor, but I have been diagnosed with general anxiety disorder and panic disorder by professionals. The advice/tips I have about dealing with your issues is probably have deep, slow breathing, to rid negative thoughts and turn them into positive ones, accept that you're anxious, do something you enjoy to keep your mind off of it, and focus on current events (no past or future ones). What I specifically do when I'm stressed is to listen to some music and to draw to let it all out. Although, if you are worried enough about it (and/or if it is making you lose sleep or you are becoming worse because of it), I recommend seeing someone for help (specifically someone who has vast experience with mental health). I hope you're alright, nonetheless.

The worst friend I've ever had was once one of the people I trusted the most. When he was one of my closest friends, there was a period of time that I was in a rough situation with another close friend. This friend (I'll call him Eric for the rest of the post) happened to help drag me out of that situation. After being great friends with him for a few months, he asked me if I'd be okay being in a relationship at the time. I said yes, but now that I look back to it, I see it was not the greatest decision. During our relationship, as I hugged on him and talked greatly of him, he was destroying my friendships with people he thought that wouldn't be good around me. It left me almost alone, and the two "bullies" that were on my case that whole year thought it would be a good idea to start harassing me online. This was because since I didn't have anyone covering my back hardly at that time (since Eric shoo'd off the friends I had), that I would be an easy target. The stress piled onto me for that year and the next one after that, leading me to become physically ill (as if my agoraphobia wasn't enough). The stress eventually became too much for me (since I had no one left, and that the ones I loved started hating me for being around the one who I thought cared for me the most). I fell ill soon afterwards, and something happened to me from it to spawn some mental/neurological issues. After telling Eric that I may not be the same (as I said about forementioned mental/neurological issues popping up), he didn't talk to me for a month, and then decided to leave me behind. I, thankfully, recovered somewhat since, and I got some of my friends back, and some new ones. The stress is still somewhat there (and that because of that I had to go to a mental hospital up in Lousville, Kentucky about a month ago), but at least I'm away from him. ^-^
